paper_metadata.title: Compositional effect on microstructure and properties of NbTiZr-based complex concentrated alloys

evidence.quote: Compositional effect on microstructure and properties of NbTiZr-based complex concentrated alloys
The results of the present work indicate that single-phase BCC microstructure is a rarity in the studied refractory high entropy alloys.

Compositional effect on phase composition, phase stability, microstructure and mechanical properties of NbTiZr-based com- plex concentrated alloys was studied using six near-equiatomic refractory alloys, NbTiZr, NbTiZrV, NbTiZrVMo, NbTiZrVTa, NbTiZrVCr, and NbTiZrVAl0.24, produced by arc melting followed by HIP and homogenized annealing.

parameters.atmosphere: low pressure high-purity argon additionally purified with a Ti getter

evidence.quote: Alloys were prepared from high purity (>99.9%) elements by vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled Cu hearth. A low pressure high-purity argon atmosphere additionally purified with a Ti getter was used to produce the arc. To ensure complete dissolution and mixing of the alloying elements in liquid state, each sample was flipped-over and re-melted at least five times. The weight of each sample was 200 g and the sample dimensions were approximately 100 mm × 30 mm x 12 mm, with rounded surfaces.

The solidified alloys, except one containing Cr, were hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) by holding at 1400 °C for 2 h under a pressure of 276 MPa of high-purity argon to close solidification porosity and then additionally annealed in high-purity argon at 1400 °C for 6 h.

The solidified alloys, except one containing Cr, were hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) by holding at 1400 °C for 2 h under a pressure of 276 MPa of high-purity argon to close solidification porosity and then additionally annealed in high-purity argon at 1400 °C for 6 h. The Cr-containing alloy was HIP'd and annealed at 1200 °C, and the annealing time was 24 h. During heat treatment, all the samples were wrapped (each individually) in a Ta foil. The heating and cooling rates were ~20 °C/min.

attributes.composition: Zr-depleted, slightly enriched with other elements

evidence.quote: Discontinuous dendrites (grey-colored in BSE images) were depleted in Zr and slightly enriched with other elements. ... one can conclude that the Zr-depleted dendrites have the BCC1 crystal structure with a = 326.0 pm

attributes.composition: rich in Ti and Zr, depleted in Mo and V

evidence.quote: Continuous (bright-color) channels (i.e. inter-dendrite regions) between the dendrites were rich in Ti and Zr and depleted in Mo and V. ... the Zr-rich channels have the BCC2 crystal structure with a = 342.4 pm

attributes.location: mainly inside channels, finer inside dendrites
attributes.composition: rich in Mo, V and Zr; (Mo,V)2Zr

evidence.quote: Finely, near-globular-shaped bright precipitates were located mainly inside the channels, but finer precipitates were also found inside the dendrites. These particles were rich in Mo, V and Zr. ... the Mo, V and Zr rich precipitates are the (Mo,V)2Zr cubic Laves phase (C15).
NbTiZrVTa had an essentially single-phase BCC equiaxed grain structure (Fig. 5a). The average grain size was 48 μm.

Chemical analysis showed that the bright-color phase was rich in Nb and Ti, while the dark-color phase was rich in Cr and V (Table 1). EBSD analysis showed that bright regions had a BCC crystal structure and dark regions had an FCC crystal structure. ... The volume fractions of the BCC and Laves phases are 0.4 and 0.6, respectively.

attributes.composition: rich in Cr and V; based on Cr2Zr

evidence.quote: Chemical analysis showed that the bright-color phase was rich in Nb and Ti, while the dark-color phase was rich in Cr and V (Table 1). EBSD analysis showed that bright regions had a BCC crystal structure and dark regions had an FCC crystal structure. Relating these findings to the X-ray diffraction data (Table 2) it was concluded that the dark-color phase is a cubic (C15) Laves phase, based on Cr2Zr, with V (and probably some Nb) taking Cr sites and Ti (and some Nb) taking Zr sites.

attributes.composition: rich in Ti and Nb, depleted in V

evidence.quote: The microstructure of NbTiZrVAl0.24 consisted of equiaxed grains of the BCC phase with secondary phases precipitated inside grains in the form of needles and at grain boundaries as a continuous layer (Fig. 7a and b). ... Chemical analysis showed that the BCC grains were rich in Ti and Nb and depleted in V (Table 1).

attributes.location: inside grains and at grain boundaries
attributes.composition: rich in V, Zr and Al; suggested formula (Al,Nb,V)2(Ti,Zr)

evidence.quote: The EBSD phase map showed that the precipitates had a hexagonal (Laves C14 [15]) crystal structure (Fig. 7c). ... Based on the measured composition and literature data [15], it is suggested that the Laves phase has a formula (Al,Nb,V)2(Ti,Zr). The volume fraction of the BCC matrix phase and precipitates were estimated to be ~0.64 and 0.36, respectively.
